topic: Simultaneous selected-training TWSF conditional-mean bands with a variance-share Gaussian-complexity frontier. Condition on latent factors and assignments in balanced, strongly identified fixed-rank panels with independent homoskedastic Gaussian cell errors, deterministic direct and recursive training cells, one common terminal W block and forecast origin, and selected-design recovery through H. Derive stacked orthogonal scores and observable positive-semidefinite Gram covariance estimates; prove uniform feasible multiplier-band coverage when (kappa+1)epsilon+(kappa+1)^2t+d tends to zero, with explicit PCR/Riesz/Jacobian rates admitting H=floor(n^(1/8)). Let nu_min be the minimum standardized variance share of independent direct lead responses. Prove bounded recursive complexity and direct complexity comparable to 1+sqrt(nu_min log(2H)) on the declared fixed-rank class. On the persistent all-ones subclass, prove kappa_rec tends to sqrt(2/pi), kappa_dir/sqrt(log H) tends to one, and probability and expected maximum-width lower bounds for uniformly honest rectangles centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator. Consumer: mlsynth TWSF path ribbons and Shen's NFL-stadium conditional-mean paths; exclude prediction bands and unrestricted-estimator minimax claims. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The stacked S12/S13 score and Gram-covariance formulas were derived. On the legal common-origin all-ones sequence, alpha*=1_L/L, J_ell'1=c_ell1, ||g_ell||^2=1/L+O(H/L^2), direct independent variance share is 1/(2+3/n), kappa_rec approaches sqrt(2/pi), and kappa_dir/sqrt(log H) approaches one. A conditional Gaussian event and sixteen-term remainder ledger yield epsilon_rec=O(H log(nH)/sqrt(n)+H^2 log(nH)/n) and normalized correlation error O_p(H^2 sqrt(log(nH)/n)), so H=n^(1/8) is nonempty. Checks covered selected-training failure, vanishing shares, singular correlations, studentization, long horizons, prediction shocks, randomized widths, and prior-art collapse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Package the displayed events into one class-uniform conditional probability bound with constants depending only on declared class radii, independently auditing spectral perturbation and exceptional-event conventions. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the three-piece perturbation bound for qhat_ell=Zhat_dagger Jhat_ell' W' betahat and the actual-PCR relative covariance rate on the all-ones sequence; pivot if an order-one normalized term or oracle W/Jacobian is required. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_twsf_path_complexity_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can direct-versus-recursive TWSF training selected on the observed panel admit one feasible multiplier band with class-uniform simultaneous conditional-mean coverage over a growing horizon, including local training-risk ties and singular stacked covariance?

source_refs.claim: TWSF supplies orthogonalized direct and recursive estimators with pointwise inference for fixed multi-step horizons, not a growing-horizon simultaneous band.
source_refs.author: Dennis Shen

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous bands after model selection for many parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores.
source_refs.author: Alexandre Belloni, Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Ying Wei

source_refs.claim: Residual-bootstrap intervals are proved for individual treated unit-time effects in an interactive-fixed-effects panel, not for joint growing paths.
source_refs.author: Xingyu Li, Yan Shen, and Qiankun Zhou

source_refs.excerpt: publication-level uniform joint Gaussian/HAC mapping over singular stacked covariances remains open.
Add uniform covariance-tail/stabilization conditions sufficient for the stated supremum over whole arrays.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest TWSF result is pointwise with a fixed horizon, while generic post-selection band theory begins with an already controlled family of estimated orthogonal scores. TWSF leads instead share estimated unit-side PCR, time-side PCR or recursive Jacobians, Riesz maps, and a terminal W block. The prior proximal-SC proposal shows that even a binary selected-coordinate problem leaves the uniform Gaussian mapping unresolved when covariance changes rank. Here the proof must additionally control an H-dimensional discontinuous selected-design map near local training ties and establish conditional multiplier approximation directly from an observable PSD Gram matrix without covariance inversion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable stacked selected-score construction and observable PSD Gram estimator, accompanied by a class-uniform conditional coverage theorem whose explicit error bound vanishes when (kappa+1)epsilon+(kappa+1)^2t+d=o(1) under primitive PCR, Riesz, Jacobian, selection, and horizon rates permitting H=floor(n^(1/8)).

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its prospective-policy motivation, latent temporal structure, direct-versus-recursive formulation, and NFL-stadium application, then isolate the distinction between pointwise intervals and an honest selected path ribbon.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Retrospective synthetic controls do not answer prospective treatment questions -> low-rank temporal structure makes treated conditional-mean forecasting possible -> TWSF gives direct and recursive pointwise inference -> users need one selected-training simultaneous ribbon for the full path

method_exemplars.technique: Construct approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores uniformly over many targets, estimate their covariance from score contributions, and prove multiplier validity through uniform linearization and high-dimensional Gaussian approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each TWSF lead is a moment-defined causal forecast with estimated nuisances, making its many-target score argument the nearest general template for stacked path bands.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove Gaussian and multiplier approximation for high-dimensional hyperrectangles without requiring nonsingular coordinate correlation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A TWSF ribbon is a hyperrectangle event for a growing, strongly correlated vector once the panel-specific score expansion and covariance approximation are established.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine factor-based completion, residual resampling, and explicit factor-estimation error control to obtain feasible causal-panel intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest panel-specific blueprint for propagating estimated-factor uncertainty, although its coordinatewise target must be replaced by a selected stacked TWSF path.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the covariance of stacked direct and recursive TWSF orthogonal scores be estimated in relative max norm using the actual selected PCR, Riesz, W-block, and recursive-Jacobian estimates, without oracle objects, for H=floor(n^(1/8))?

source_refs.claim: TWSF derives pointwise variance estimators for orthogonalized PCR forecasts under fixed-horizon asymptotics.
source_refs.author: Dennis Shen

source_refs.claim: PCR receives nonasymptotic fixed-design errors-in-variables and out-of-sample prediction guarantees applicable to synthetic controls.
source_refs.author: Anish Agarwal, Devavrat Shah, and Dennis Shen

source_refs.claim: Entrywise low-rank-completion inference is established using an auxiliary leave-one-out proof device rather than implemented sample splitting.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao

source_refs.excerpt: Weak factors, rank uncertainty, a growing horizon, and a growing path menu are excluded.

open_problems.why_unsolved: PCR prediction bounds do not control every studentized covariance entry after multiplication by estimated unit weights, horizon-specific loadings, Riesz maps, the shared W block, and recursive Jacobian products. Pointwise variance consistency absorbs fixed-dimensional errors, but a growing-H multiplier band requires max-norm correlation control even near singularity. The prior Synthetic-Blips proposal likewise obtained only a finite-depth replay recursion and explicitly excluded a growing horizon. Its fixed-depth induction must become an H-growing operator perturbation argument that tracks shared innovations and Jacobian accumulation while using the implemented, selected PCR objects rather than oracle W or Jacobians.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable PSD Gram estimator and uniform perturbation theorem decomposing qhat_ell-q_ell into selected-PCR design, Riesz, W-block, and Jacobian errors, proving normalized covariance error O_p(H^2 sqrt(log(nH)/n)) or sharper and exhibiting a fixed-rank failure sequence beyond the admissible horizon-information frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Frame this as closing the feasibility gap between pointwise plug-in variance and a software-ready simultaneous path covariance constructed from the same PCR and Riesz objects.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Orthogonalized TWSF enables pointwise inference -> a path ribbon needs the full cross-lead covariance -> that covariance reuses estimated PCR and recursive objects -> an actual-estimator Gram rate is the inferential last mile

method_exemplars.technique: Control hard-truncated PCR through fixed-design subspace perturbation and explicit span conditions while retaining prediction-direction rather than only Frobenius error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every TWSF covariance loading is an out-of-sample linear functional of an estimated low-rank PCR system, so direction-specific perturbation is the first required Gram-rate step.

method_exemplars.technique: Introduce an auxiliary leave-one-out estimator in the proof to separate factor-estimation dependence from target-cell noise, then prove equivalence to the implemented full-sample estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Stacked TWSF scores reuse cells in their low-rank nuisances and covariance contributions, creating the same dependence problem without authorizing a different implemented estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert entrywise covariance approximation into stability of Gaussian maximum laws and critical values via comparison and anti-concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested correlation rate matters because it must stabilize the multiplier maximum even when the limiting covariance is singular.

open_problems.open_problem: How does the minimum standardized share nu_min of independent direct-lead noise determine the Gaussian maximum complexity of direct TWSF relative to recursive TWSF on the declared strongly identified fixed-rank class?

source_refs.claim: TWSF develops direct horizon-specific and recursive forecasts but does not characterize their pathwise Gaussian complexities.
source_refs.author: Dennis Shen

source_refs.claim: The paper proves comparison and anti-concentration inequalities for maxima of Gaussian vectors with arbitrary covariance matrices.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: Gaussian and multiplier approximations are developed for maxima of high-dimensional vector sums, including strongly correlated coordinates.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic Gaussian comparison theory describes maxima through the entire canonical covariance metric, while TWSF separates direct and recursive procedures only at the estimator level. No located paper identifies a panel-structural scalar that forces direct coordinates apart while recursive coordinates remain nearly common. Proving that nu_min is such a scalar requires a TWSF covariance decomposition, a uniform bound on recursive Jacobian propagation, and a Gaussian-separation argument showing that lead-specific direct innovations create sqrt(log H) growth; the search found no result combining those steps for causal forecast paths.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A covariance-structural characterization proving uniformly bounded recursive Gaussian complexity and two-sided direct complexity comparable to 1+sqrt(nu_min log(2H)), plus a legal persistent all-ones fixed-rank sequence on which kappa_rec converges to sqrt(2/pi) and kappa_dir/sqrt(log H) converges to one.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its side-by-side direct and recursive constructions to motivate why estimators with comparable pointwise theory can have sharply different simultaneous uncertainty costs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: TWSF offers direct and recursive multi-step forecasts -> pointwise asymptotics hide cross-lead dependence -> simultaneous ribbons depend on Gaussian maxima rather than marginal variances -> independent variance share may expose a direct-versus-recursive complexity frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration to relate TWSF correlation geometry to maximum quantiles and expected maxima.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired frontier is explicitly a statement about maxima of centered Gaussian vectors under two structured covariance geometries.

method_exemplars.technique: Smooth the maximum, couple the score maximum to a covariance-matched Gaussian vector, and transfer its critical value to multiplier inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery links the structural Gaussian-complexity comparison to the critical value of a feasible simultaneous TWSF band.

open_problems.open_problem: Are sqrt(log H)-scale maximum widths unavoidable for every uniformly honest rectangle centered at the direct leading-Gaussian TWSF estimator when nu_min is bounded away from zero, including data-dependent, asymmetric, or randomized widths?

source_refs.claim: TWSF's pointwise confidence intervals do not establish necessity or optimality of multiplicity inflation for an entire forecast path.
source_refs.author: Dennis Shen

source_refs.claim: The paper proves expected-width lower bounds for honest confidence bands and treats random band size.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Mark G. Low, and Zongming Ma
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Gaussian anti-concentration supports honest multiplier confidence bands without requiring a limiting extreme-value law.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.excerpt: LAN weak convergence alone does not transfer simultaneous coverage and worst-case expected maximum width.
Add explicit deficiencies, a bounded-loss truncation lemma, and a coverage-deficit repair construction.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing honest-band lower bounds concern nonparametric function classes, whereas TWSF produces a finite but growing Gaussian rectangle whose covariance is constrained by the panel construction. Gaussian-max theory supplies critical values but not an estimator-centered causal-panel width lower bound. The prior predictor-risk proposal identifies a further proof boundary: weak convergence to a Gaussian experiment does not transfer claims quantified over arbitrary randomized bands because coverage indicators are discontinuous and maximum width is unbounded. A valid TWSF argument must embed a persistent fixed-rank subclass, preserve common-origin and training restrictions, and use either parameter-independent comparison kernels or a direct finite-sample reduction with truncation and coverage repair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Uniform probability and expected maximum-width lower bounds showing that every honest rectangle centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator has maximum width at least c_alpha sqrt(nu_min log H) on a persistent all-ones subclass, with the conclusion extended to data-dependent, asymmetric, and randomized widths through a valid experiment-transfer or direct finite-sample argument.

writing_exemplar.why: Keep the lower bound tied to the prospective conditional-mean path and direct TWSF estimator used in applications rather than presenting an unrestricted-estimator minimax claim.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Applied TWSF displays a horizon path -> pointwise intervals do not jointly cover that path -> direct leads retain independent innovations -> honest rectangles centered at the direct estimator may necessarily pay a sqrt(log H) width cost

method_exemplars.technique: Translate uniform honesty into testing constraints and lower-bound the expected width of random confidence bands over a carefully chosen finite subfamily.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result also concerns unavoidable expected and probabilistic width for possibly randomized bands, but its finite subfamily must remain inside the declared TWSF class.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian comparison, canonical-metric separation, and anti-concentration to turn a nonvanishing independent variance share into a sharp maximum scale.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The direct leading error on the persistent subclass is Gaussian, making its correlated maximum the decisive lower-bound object.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian decision geometry and modulus arguments to connect honest coverage with sharp expected-length lower bounds and attaining procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a proof architecture for transferring a Gaussian benchmark to honest inferential width while keeping the estimator and parameter class explicit.

literature_map:
Shen (2026, arXiv:2606.18512) is the exact anchor: TWSF identifies prospective treated conditional means and gives orthogonalized pointwise inference for fixed direct and recursive horizons.
The accompanying mlsynth materials expose pointwise path intervals and cross-validated hyperparameters, underscoring the gap between displayed ribbons and simultaneous coverage.
Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, JMLR; arXiv:2010.14449) provide fixed-design PCR identification and out-of-sample prediction bounds, but not covariance estimation for a growing causal-forecast vector.
Agarwal, Shah, Shen, and Song (2021, JASA; arXiv:1902.10920) establish robust PCR/HSVT guarantees and the PCR-robust-synthetic-control equivalence.
Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2202.12078) give residual-bootstrap intervals for individual treated unit-time effects in interactive-factor panels.
Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2307.16370) obtain entrywise low-rank-completion inference through an auxiliary leave-one-out proof.
Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA; arXiv:2308.02364) provide debiased inference under structured nonrandom missingness but do not treat prospective recursive paths.
Athey et al. (2021, JASA; arXiv:1710.10251) develop causal matrix completion and leave asymptotic confidence-interval theory outside the original paper's scope.
Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Wei (2018, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1512.07619) give the closest generic template for simultaneous post-selection bands from orthogonal scores.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1212.6906) supply Gaussian and multiplier approximation for high-dimensional maxima.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, PTRF; arXiv:1301.4807) supply arbitrary-covariance comparison and anti-concentration, including singular cases.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2017, Annals of Probability; arXiv:1412.3661) extend CLT and bootstrap validity to high-dimensional hyperrectangles.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1303.7152) connect anti-concentration to honest multiplier bands without an extreme-value limit.
Cai, Low, and Ma (2014, JASA; DOI:10.1080/01621459.2013.879260) provide expected-width lower-bound machinery for honest random bands, but in nonparametric regression rather than TWSF.
The unresolved intersection is panel-specific: selected shared PCR, Riesz, W-block, and Jacobian nuisances must be linearized jointly, their observable Gram matrix controlled for growing H, and direct-versus-recursive Gaussian geometry converted into coverage and width limits.
